label: copy-phase input i near the end of short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input is the letter i (99.5% of activation mass is on input i; never in the original or delimiter phases). Within copy-phase i inputs it is strongly position-graded: it is strongest when i is one of the last two tokens being copied back (to_go <= 1) in short sequences (L = 4-5 carry ~83% of mass), with top activations at recall step 3 of L=4 sequences (e.g. c t i i <DEL> c t [i]). Copy-phase i in long sequences (L >= 7), or early in the copy (recall_idx <= 1), is mostly inactive or very weak. The identity of the output token or earlier tokens has little effect. The bare rule copy-phase in_tok == i has mass recall 0.995 but precision 0.17; adding to_go <= 1 and L <= 6 gives dev F1 0.70 and mass recall 0.89, but the position/length dependence is graded, so no sharp boundary exists.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, u, d, h, r, p; least: f, w, y, b) and the token being output (most: i, d, h, u, r, p; least: q, e, z, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3, L=4 & t=7.
